title: Neutrophil profiling illuminates anti-tumor antigen-presenting potency
one_line: Single-cell profiling of tumor-infiltrating neutrophils defined 10 neutrophil states and identified an HLA-DR+ antigen-presenting state, driven by leucine metabolism, that can present tumor neoantigens and activate T cells.
key_claims: Ten distinct neutrophil states were identified within the tumor microenvironment, one of them an antigen-presenting state marked by HLA-DR expression.
HLA-DR+ neutrophils present tumor neoantigens and activate T cell responses, positioning them as alternative antigen-presenting cells.
Leucine metabolism activates the antigen-presenting program in neutrophils, suggesting a metabolic switch that could be targeted therapeutically.
Neutrophils are proposed as attractive APCs because of their abundance, rapid response, phagocytic capacity and short lifespan.
HLA-DR+ neutrophils can also activate T cells in an antigen-independent manner.
limitations: Relatively small sample size; findings need validation in larger cohorts.
Potential adverse effects of a leucine-rich diet were not investigated.
Mechanism of antigen-independent T cell activation by HLA-DR+ neutrophils remains unexplained.
No clinical translation shown; leucine delivery methods remain undefined.
No specific effect sizes or quantitative outcomes reported in the show notes.
open_questions: Can neutrophils be deliberately reprogrammed into the HLA-DR+ antigen-presenting state in vivo, and does this improve tumor control?
Is leucine supplementation safe and effective in preclinical and clinical settings?
What mechanism underlies antigen-independent T cell activation by HLA-DR+ neutrophils?
Do the 10 neutrophil states replicate across larger, independent patient cohorts and tumor types?
